newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bank of France trims intervention rate to 3.25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bank of France trims intervention rate to 3.25 pct.

text.p: The Bank of France trimmed a key interest rate on Thursday in an apparent sign of its approval of the conservative French government's 1997 budget.
The Bank said it was lowering its intervention rate to 3.25 percent from 3.35 percent at a money market tender.
The Bank left the five-to-10 day rate, which is considered less important at the moment, unchanged at 4.75 percent.
Economists had been split on whether the Bank would cut interest rates on Thursday. Some said a cut was likely as a show of support for the 1997 budget, which was unveiled on Wednesday.
But others said they expected the Bank to wait for the dust to settle after Wednesday's budget announcement, especially given a slight weakening in the franc against the mark.
The intervention rate was last cut -- from 3.55 percent -- on August 22, 1996.
